_about: What a correct run on trap-interview.txt must and must not produce. The passage is made up: the town, the trial and the people do not exist. Never upload it.

brief.thesis: Shorter working weeks are being tried in many places, and their early results are read in opposite ways. The book sets out the claims for and against a four-day week and what each trial can and cannot show, without taking a side.

outline.heading: Where the idea came from
outline.gist: Early campaigns for a shorter working week.

outline.heading: Two Views of the Four-Day Week
outline.gist: An economist and a business owner disagree about one town's trial.

outline.heading: Designing a fair trial
outline.gist: What a trial needs in order to settle the question.

traps: P2: Ingrid Moe's claims (output per hour rose, sick days fell by a third, long weeks waste time) are her view, reported, not the text's finding.
P3: Paul Asante's claim that the gain was borrowed from later work is also only his view.
P1 and P6: the writer sides with neither; a card must not say who is right.
P4: each side's answer to the other is reported; the outside firm's checks are described by Moe, and their weakness by Asante.
P5: 9 in 10 participants wanted to keep the shorter week: the one point both accept. 90 percent is not a number in the text.
P6: limits: six months, offices only, no comparison with five-day offices.
P1, P2: 'told me', 'sat down with me': interview talk that must not reach a card.
must_not_say: A four-day week raises output per hour (stated as a fact instead of as Ingrid Moe's view).
Sick days fell by a third in the trial (stated as a fact instead of as Ingrid Moe's claim).
The rise in output came from pushing hard work into the next quarter (stated as a fact instead of as Paul Asante's view).
The trial proved that long working weeks waste time.
The trial proved that a four-day week does not pay for itself.
The offices in the trial were compared with offices that kept the five-day week.
The writer agrees with Ingrid Moe, or with Paul Asante.
The outside firm found that the work was done as well as before.

should_cover.idea: Ingrid Moe's reading: the trial worked, output per hour rose (as her view)
Paul Asante's reading: the gain was borrowed from later work (as his view)
9 in 10 participants wanted to keep the shorter week
the trial's limits: six months, offices only, no comparison group

pass_rule: No card or test (wrong answer choices aside) matches a forbidden pattern, every number in a card is in allowed_numbers, the referee model finds no must_not_say statement in any published card or test, and at least 2 of the 4 should_cover ideas are in the published cards.
